The last two steps require SPF and DKIM | CIS.M365.2.1.8, CISA.MS.EXO.2.2 · CIS.M365.2.1.9, CISA.MS.EXO.3.1, ORCA.108, ORCA.108.1 · CISA.MS.EXO.4.1 · ORCA.235 · CIS.M365.2.1.10 · CISA.MS.EXO.4.2, MT.1182 |
595	| `defender-device-risk` Use Defender device risk in compliance (5) | `intune.defender-connector` → `intune.defender-compliance-evaluation` · `defender.endpoint-onboarding` and `intune.compliance-policies` (recommended first) → `intune.compliance-device-risk` | unchecked · unchecked (ZTA.24871, Android only) · unchecked (ZTA.41045) · see `compliant-devices` · MT.1231 |
596	
597	The count after each goal includes the foundation steps it reaches. A step can count in several goals, so the
598	counts add up to more than 43.
599	
600	### Changes from the draft
601	
602	- **A new goal, `managed-devices`.** A compliant or hybrid joined device is something Learn offers organizations
603	  that aren't ready to require compliance for everyone (policy-all-users-device-compliance). It is another end
604	  state, not a step towards compliant devices. It is also what CIS 5.2.2.9 and CISA 3.7 ask for. MT.1014 covers
605	  admin roles only, so it gets its own step, `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins`. Learn offers the admin
606	  policy first, so that step is recommended first. `entra.hybrid-join` is new and Unchecked. Graph shows which
607	  devices are hybrid joined, but not the domain PCs that aren't.
608	- **Foundation.** `entra.emergency-access-accounts` is new. Learn's prerequisite for PIM is that the accounts
609	  exist and keep Global Administrator as a permanent active assignment (security-emergency-access,
610	  pim-deployment-plan). That is a different fact from their Conditional Access exclusion. The same page creates
611	  the accounts before it excludes them, so the new step is recommended before `entra.emergency-access-excluded`.
612	- **Risk policies.**
613	  - Password writeback is required only for the user-risk policy. Sign-in risk is cleared with MFA
614	    (howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies).
615	  - Password hash sync and remediating existing high-risk users are recommended before the user-risk policy. Learn
616	    puts the review first in its deployment plan (how-to-deploy-identity-protection) and ties leaked-credential
617	    detection to password hash sync (id-protection-faq).
618	  - The goal ends at `entra.ca-user-risk`, with the sign-in risk policy recommended first. Unremediated sign-in risk
619	    raises user risk (howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock).
620	  - Learn's rule that the two risk conditions go in separate policies is a warning, not an order. It is now in both
621	    steps' rollout, so `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate` and MT.1049 left the catalogue.
622	  - `entra.trusted-named-locations` (CIS 5.2.2.14) is new and recommended before sign-in risk. Some detections use
623	    trusted locations to cut false positives.
624	  - `entra.ca-user-risk` is `Unchecked`. Learn now recommends the Require risk remediation grant (policy-risk-based-user),
625	    and MT.1013 and CIS 5.2.2.6 accept only Require password change.
626	- **Phishing-resistant MFA.**
627	  - Windows Hello for Business is one of the methods that meet the phishing-resistant strength, not a link in the
628	    chain (concept-authentication-strengths). It is now `intune.windows-hello`, in a "one of" group with passkeys,
629	    certificate-based authentication and macOS Platform SSO. A tenant that uses only one of them is not blocked.
630	  - Registration is split into admins and all users, and enforcement requires each. Learn warns that an
631	    unregistered admin can lock the tenant out (policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa).
632	  - The Temporary Access Pass is one of two ways to bootstrap registration, so it is recommended first, not
633	    required.
634	  - Admins come first "typically", so the admin policy is recommended before the all-users one, not required.
635	- **Privileged access.**
636	  - The draft's `entra.pim-alerts` became `entra.pim-notifications`. CISA 7.7 checks notification recipients, not
637	    PIM security alerts.
638	  - `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (CIS 5.3.4, CISA 7.6) is new. It requires the emergency access accounts,
639	    because approval with no available approver locks the tenant (pim-how-to-change-default-settings).
640	  - Learn sets role settings before it hands out eligible assignments (pim-getting-started), so both settings steps
641	    are recommended first.
642	  - `entra.pim-roles-used` (MT.1030) left the goal. Learn treats unused roles as an alert to act on and access
643	    reviews as the prevention, not as a rollout step.
644	- **Token protection.** The step is `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`, because every test checks a Windows
645	  policy and Learn deploys Apple separately with its own prerequisites. Device registration is recommended first,
646	  not required: current Windows builds prompt unregistered users to register (deployment-guide-token-protection-windows).
647	  The same guide pairs the policy with blocking unknown platforms, which MT.1015 checks.
648	- **Email authentication.**
649	  - The steps are `defender.*`. Learn documents them under Defender for Office 365, DKIM is set up in the Defender
650	    portal, and most of the tests declare `defender`.
651	  - SPF and DKIM are required only by the steps that enforce DMARC. A p=none record changes no delivery, and Learn
652	    advises publishing one early to find senders (email-authentication-spf-configure).
653	  - `dmarc-monitor` became `defender.dmarc-published` (CISA 4.1).
654	  - CIS 2.1.10 rejects p=none, so it verifies `defender.dmarc-enforce`, which means quarantine or reject with
655	    reports on every domain, as the deployment guide asks (mdo-deployment-guide).
656	  - The goal ends at p=reject (`defender.dmarc-reject`, CISA 4.2 and MT.1182).
657	  - ORCA.235 fails `~all`, so it verifies its own step, `defender.spf-hard-fail`.
658	- **Defender device risk.**
659	  - Learn connects the services before it onboards devices, so the draft order is reversed.
660	  - The connector's per-platform compliance toggle is a step of its own (configure-integration).
661	  - Compliance policies are recommended first, not required, because the risk score is one setting inside them.
662	  - MT.1098 doesn't verify the connector (section 11). MT.1235 reads the third-party threat level on Android
663	    device administrator, not Defender's risk score. MT.1216 reads a macOS setting that Learn doesn't document.
664	    Only MT.1231 (iOS) verifies the step.
665	
666	### Tests that check a related setting but name no step
667	
668	| Tests | Why |
669	| --- | --- |
670	| MT.1013, CIS.M365.5.2.2.6 | Reject Learn's Require risk remediation grant. They name `entra.ca-user-risk` once they accept it, which needs `Prefer: include-unknown-enum-members` on the policy request |
671	| CISA.MS.AAD.2.1, CISA.MS.AAD.2.3, CIS.M365.5.2.2.8 | Block risky users or sign-ins. Learn prefers self-remediation and treats a block as a stopgap |
672	| MT.1049 | Its rule moved into the risk steps' rollout |
673	| CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 | Covers a different set of admin roles from CIS 5.2.2.5 and Learn, so the two would disagree in one run |
674	| EIDSCA.AF03–AF06, EIDSCA.AT02 | Hardening that Learn makes optional |
675	| MT.1025–MT.1028, MT.1030, CISA.MS.AAD.7.4 | Admin-account hygiene, not eligibility. CISA 7.4 also fails the permanent emergency access accounts that Learn asks for |
676	| CISA.MS.EXO.4.3 | Applies only to CISA's own reporting address |
677	| MT.1098, MT.1216, MT.1235 | See "Defender device risk" above |
678	
679	Some tagged tests check less than their step, and the step record says how many of its tests ran:
680	
681	- MT.1001 accepts any enabled policy that uses the compliant-device control.
682	- CISA 3.7 fails a stricter policy that requires compliance only.
683	- MT.1231 fails a tenant with no iOS compliance policy.
684	- CISA 7.5 fails emergency access assignments made outside PIM.
685	
686	Fixing these is test work, outside this design.
687	
688	The first catalogue has no `Conflicts` entry yet. The obvious one is security defaults. Learn says to turn them
689	off before relying on Conditional Access (security-defaults, plan-conditional-access). MT.1021 can't verify it,
690	because it checks that security defaults are on and skips any tenant with Entra ID P1 or better, which is every
691	tenant that uses Conditional Access. A measure or check of whether security defaults are off where Conditional Access is
692	licensed would make the conflict checkable. It is listed with the later measures in section 11.
693	
694	Candidates for later goals come from the research and from this pass:
695	
696	- legacy authentication, guest access, app consent and workload credentials;
697	- hybrid hardening, SSPR and LAPS;
698	- data protection, SharePoint sharing and audit;
699	- Defender for Office 365, Global Secure Access and AI agents;
700	- Copilot readiness, Insider Risk and Defender for Cloud Apps;
701	- third-party mail filters, Defender for Identity, Power Platform and Active Directory;
702	- privileged access hygiene (MT.1025–MT.1030, CIS 5.3.3), token protection on Apple devices, and third-party
703	  Mobile Threat Defense.
704	
705	## 16. Delivery
706	
707	| Milestone | Work | Needs |
708	| --- | --- | --- |
709	| M1 Format | Schema and loader (`Get-MtStepCatalog`, internal), the `Step` attribute in C#, the schema table and the reader, `StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`, and the compliant-devices goal as the fixture | This design |
710	| M2 Catalogue | Expert pass on the seven goals against the mirrors, then `Step` on about 75 tests, plus `Step` in the Zero Trust `taxonomy.json` | M1, and the instance-attribute change on `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping` |
711	| M3 Engine | `Step` on rows, reading the measures of the steps in scope, `Get-MtResultStep` (status, readiness, rank, scope), `LastKnown`, `-Step`, `-IncludePrerequisites`, `Get-MtTest -Step`, CSV and Markdown columns, the console line | M1 |
712	| M4 Report | Action plan groups and lanes, Before you fix this, rollout in How to fix, the overview card | M3's result shape. It can start on sample data once section 7 is final |
713	| M5 Measures | The measure registry, the two readers of section 11, and `Measure` on their steps | M1 for the format. The readers can be written before it |
714	| M6 Tooling | `build/steps/` scripts and the weekly workflow | M1 |
715	| M7 Docs and site | `Step` in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`, a defender's path page, and one page per goal on maester.dev built by `prepare-data.mjs` | M2 |
716	
717	Once M1 lands, M2, M5 and M6 touch different files and can run in parallel sessions. M3 and M4 follow in order.
718	
719	## 17. Decisions
720	
721	The owner accepted the recommended answer to each decision on 5 November 2026, and changed decision 10 later that day.
722	Three rulings on the measures followed: `devices-compliant` declares the Intune licence, because only Intune marks
723	devices compliant; a registry entry may carry a `Caveat`; and the MFA measure counts `isMfaCapable`.
724	
725	| # | Decision | Ruling | Alternatives considered |
726	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
727	| 1 | Name readers see | **Defender's path**, the counterpart of an attack path | "Implementation order", "Do this first" |
728	| 2 | Attribute name | **`Step`** | `Change` (clashes with the report's Changes page and with drift), `Prerequisite` (says the opposite of what most tests are) |
729	| 3 | What a lane is called | **Goal** (`Goals` in the result) | "Path", which clashes with `-Path` on `Invoke-Maester` and `Get-MtTest` and with file paths in the result |
730	| 4 | Where the catalogue lives | **`powershell/assets/steps/`**, beside the taxonomy, with no build change | A top-level `steps/` folder like `packs/`, which is easier to find but needs a build copy and a layout rule. Not under `tests/`, which holds only suites |
731	| 5 | Statuses | **Done, Not done, Unknown, Not checked, Not applicable** | Only Done and Not done, which turns every gap into a failure |
732	| 6 | Investigate | **Counts as Unknown** | Counts as Not done |
733	| 7 | Conflicts | **Block** while the conflicting step is on, declared on the step that needs the other off | Warn only |
734	| 8 | Selectors | **`-Step` and `-IncludePrerequisites`**, no goal selector, no new public command | A `Get-MtStep` command, which would add public API to keep |
735	| 9 | Packs and custom tests | **May name built-in steps.** Their own catalogues come later | Built-in tests only |
736	| 10 | Prerequisites that are tenant states | **Measures: figures read from Graph for the steps in scope, with `MinimumShare` (default 95) on the step and a run config override.** Changed from tests with a `MinimumShare` parameter | New tests, which would add findings with no real severity and change pass rates |
737	| 11 | Earlier statuses | **`LastKnown` per test, read only when a step in scope is Not checked** | The newest earlier run only, which says little after a one-check run |
738	| 12 | Catalogue wording | **Maester's own words and a link, 200 characters at most** | Quoting Learn |
739	| 13 | Mining output | **Proposals for review, and a weekly issue for changed sources** | A workflow that opens pull requests |
740	| 14 | Fact keys | **Ask the facts work for `Key` and a raw value before it ships** | Add them later. That breaks nothing, but costs more |
741	| 15 | Action plan | **The defender's path leads the page, with the ranked list below** | A separate page, which keeps today's plan unchanged but hides the strong point |
742	
743	## 18. Not in this design
744	
745	- The insights step (`Insight.<ID>.ps1`), attack scenarios, the most exposed identities and the reader profile.
746	  They are the rest of Phase 1 and get a design of their own. Steps are the same unit as the planned "fix once,
747	  close many" groups, so that work reuses this catalogue.
748	- Custom step catalogues for users and packs.
749	- Measured user impact from sign-in logs and report-only results. It would add measures later.
750	- Goals for GitHub, Azure DevOps and Active Directory. Until they exist, those runs look as they do today.
751	- A model that decides pass, fail, severity or order. Order comes from the catalogue, and every relationship
752	  cites its source.

﻿function Get-MtResultFramework {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Builds the Frameworks list of a result: the catalogue of each framework the rows map to.

    .DESCRIPTION
    A row names requirements through Benchmark and Control, but a report also needs the requirements that no
    test checks and a framework's name, version and size, so that it can show coverage. For each framework
    key the rows use, this returns Key, Name, Version, Url, Complete and Requirements.

    - A framework that ships with Maester (Get-MtBuiltInFramework) lists every requirement with its facts
      (Level, Profile, Criticality, Strategy, Guideline, Section and so on), without Related and Tests. A
      catalogue larger than -MaxRequirements (the ISM) lists only the requirements the rows name, and
      Complete is $false.
    - NIST SP 800-53 (assets/MaesterNistControls.json) lists only the controls the rows name, with Title and
      Family, and Complete is $false: a run is never meant to cover the whole catalogue.
    - A framework key that neither knows (one declared by a custom suite) has no entry.

    Frameworks are listed in the order Maester ships them, then NIST.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # Result rows with Benchmark and Control.
        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $InputObject = @(),

        # The largest catalogue that is listed in full.
        [Parameter()] [int] $MaxRequirements = 300
    )

    $ignoreCase = [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    # Framework key to the requirement IDs the rows name.
    $used = [System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary[string, System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]]::new($ignoreCase)
    $add = {
        param($key, $id)
        if (-not $key -or -not $id) { return }
        if (-not $used.ContainsKey($key)) { $used[$key] = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::Ordinal) }

13:produce a verdict, has a `ReasonCode` and a human-readable `ReasonDetail` on its row. This page explains how
22:$plan.Tests | Group-Object Result, ReasonCode | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Format-Table Count, Name
128:| `TestSkipped` | The test skipped itself with `-SkippedBecause` for another reason. The 2.x code (for example `NotSupportedAppPermission`) is in `ResultDetail.TestSkipped`. | Read `ReasonDetail`. |

and `Investigate` rows have no reason code. The reason codes below are a closed list.

### NotRun

The test was not run because of what you asked for.

| Reason code | Meaning | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DisabledByConfig` | A `TestSettings` row sets `"Enabled": false`. `ReasonDetail` is the row's `Reason`, if any. | Remove the row or set `Enabled` to `true`. |
| `NotListed` | `Selection.DefaultAction` is `Skip` and no `TestSettings` row sets `"Enabled": true` for this test (or, for a family, for its parent or any instance). | Add `{ "Id": "<ID>", "Enabled": true }`, or use `DefaultAction: Run`. |
| `ExcludedById` | The ID matches `-ExcludeTestId` or `Selection.ExcludeTestId`. | Remove the pattern. |
| `ExcludedByProduct` | The test's `Product` or one of its `RelatedProduct` values matches `-ExcludeProduct` or `Selection.ExcludeProduct`. A test with no product, such as a Pester-format test, is never excluded this way. | Remove the product from the exclusions. |
| `NotSelected` | `-TestId` (or `Selection.TestId`) was given and does not match this test, or `-Tag` was given and none of the tags selects the test, or the test does not match one of `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Severity` and `-Suite`; `ReasonDetail` names that selector. For a family, an instance that a `-TestId` naming other instances did not cover. A Pester-format test is `NotSelected` whenever the run selects by product, feature or area, because it has none. | Add the ID, value or tag, or drop the filter. |
| `ExcludedByTag` | A tag in `-ExcludeTag`, `Selection.ExcludeTag` or `PesterConfiguration.Filter.ExcludeTag` selects the test. | Remove the tag from the exclusions. |
| `Preview` | A test with `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` (in a Pester-format test, the `Preview` tag), excluded by default. | `-IncludePreview`, any `-Tag`, `Selection.IncludePreview`, or name its exact ID in `-TestId`. |
| `LongRunning` | A test with `LongRunning` (in a Pester-format test, the `LongRunning` tag), excluded by default. | `-IncludeLongRunning`, `-Tag LongRunning` or `-Tag CAWhatIf`, `Selection.IncludeLongRunning`, or name its exact ID in `-TestId`. |
| `OptInServiceNotConnected` | A test that needs an opt-in service (Active Directory, or a pack connector marked `OptIn`) that is not connected. | `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory`, or the service `ReasonDetail` names. |
| `DryRun` | `-DryRun`: the test would have run. | Run without `-DryRun`. |
| `PackUnavailable` | A test of a [Maester Pack](../packs/index.md) that cannot run on this computer: the pack or a module it needs is not in the local pack store, or its files changed after it was approved. | `Restore-MtPack`, or `Install-MtPack` again to review the change. |
| `PackNotAllowed` | The pack policy (`PackPolicy`, `MAESTER_PACK_POLICY` or the machine policy file) does not allow the pack. `ReasonDetail` names the rule. | Ask whoever sets the policy, or remove the pack. |
| `PackBlocked` | The pack is on the signed Maester Packs blocklist. `ReasonDetail` is the advisory. | Uninstall the pack. |
| `DeselectedAtRuntime` | Pester-format tests only: an instance of a test whose name is built at run time ran although the run selected other instances or excluded this one. Its result is not reported. | Nothing; select the instances you want by ID. |

A wildcard in `-TestId` does not lift the Preview and long-running exclusions; an exact ID does.

### Skipped

The test applies to some tenants but not, or not now, to this one.

| Reason code | Meaning | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ServiceNotConnected` | A service in the test's `Service` list is not connected. `ReasonDetail` names it. | Connect it, for example `Connect-Maester -Service ExchangeOnline`. |
| `ServiceNotRegistered` | A custom test names a service this Maester version does not know, or the service of a pack connector that is not installed. | Fix the name (see the [service list](../writing-tests/index.mdx#service)), install the pack, or update Maester. |
| `LicenseNotFound` | The tenant has none of the licences in `License`. | Nothing, if the licence is not in use. To force the decision, set `Environment.Licenses`, or turn the check off with `Environment.Enforce.License = false`. |
| `TenantTypeMismatch` | Tenant type is enforced and the test does not apply to this type of tenant. | Turn off `Environment.Enforce.TenantType`, or correct `Environment.TenantType`. |
| `CloudMismatch` | Cloud is enforced and the test does not apply to this cloud. | Turn off `Environment.Enforce.Cloud`, or correct `Environment.Cloud`. |
| `PlatformMismatch` | The test runs only on another operating system (for example Windows). | Run it on that operating system. |
| `NotApplicable` | The test called `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable`: it decided at run time that it does not apply. | Nothing. |
| `TestSkipped` | The test skipped itself with `-SkippedBecause` for another reason. The 2.x code (for example `NotSupportedAppPermission`) is in `ResultDetail.TestSkipped`. | Read `ReasonDetail`. |
| `NoInstances` | A family's instance source returned nothing: there is nothing in this tenant to check. | Nothing. |
| `NoResult` | The test returned `$null` without skipping. | For a custom test: return `$true` or `$false`, or skip explicitly. |

### Error

The test, its configuration or its file has a problem. Errors that Maester raises without running the test fail
the run and the CI test results; errors raised by the test itself do not, unless you set
`Output.ErrorsAsFailures` (see [Result schema](../result-schema.md#top-level-result)).

| Reason code | Raised by | Meaning | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TestError` | The test | The test threw an error or called `-SkippedBecause Error`. `ReasonDetail` is the first line of the message; `ErrorRecord` holds the full record. | Read the message. Often a missing permission or an API failure. |

﻿function Invoke-Maester {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    This is the main Maester command that runs the tests and generates a report of the results.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Using Invoke-Maester is the easiest way to run the Pester tests and generate a report of the results.

    For more advanced configuration, you can directly use the Pester module and the Get-MtHtmlReport function.

    By default, Invoke-Maester runs the tests that ship with Maester and the custom tests in the Custom folder of the current directory, except Active Directory tests, preview tests and long-running tests. With -Path, native custom tests (`Test.*.ps1`) are found anywhere under the path and Pester-format custom tests (`*.Tests.ps1`) only in a Custom folder. Folders are searched up to three levels deep. Active Directory tests run only after an explicit Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory call succeeds.

    -Product, -Feature, -Area, -Severity and -Suite select tests by their typed attributes. Each takes a list: the values of one selector are alternatives, and different selectors must all match. They combine the same way with -Tag and -TestId. -ExcludeProduct leaves out the tests of a product and wins over every selector. The tags of Maester 2.x, such as CA or CIS, still select the same built-in tests.

    .PARAMETER ExcludeProduct
    Do not run the tests of these products: keys such as entra or exchange, or an alias such as 'exo' or 'Entra ID'. Matches a test's Product or any of its RelatedProduct values, and '*' wildcards are allowed, as for -Product. Adds to Selection.ExcludeProduct in the run configuration and wins over -Product, -TestId and the other selectors. Excluded tests are reported as NotRun with the reason code ExcludedByProduct. A test without a product, such as a Pester-format custom test, is never excluded.

    .PARAMETER IncludeLongRunning
    Include tests that can take a long time to run in tenants with a large number of objects.

    .PARAMETER IncludePreview
    Include tests that are still being tested or are dependent on preview APIs.

    .PARAMETER NoLogo
    Do not show the Maester logo.

    .PARAMETER NonInteractive
    This will suppress the logo when Maester starts, prevent the test results from being opened in the default browser, and suppress all pretty messages.

    .PARAMETER OutputMode

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Invoke-Maester
    #>
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSAvoidUsingWriteHost', '', Justification = 'Colors are beautiful')]
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSReviewUnusedParameter', '', Justification = 'Incorrectly flags ExportCsv and ExportExcel as unused')]
    [Alias('Invoke-MtMaester')]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param (
        # The folder that holds your custom tests and configuration, or the path of one test file. Native tests are found
        # in any folder under it, Pester-format tests only in a Custom folder, up to three folder levels deep.
        # Without -Path, the Custom folder of the current folder is used. Wildcards are not expanded.
        [Parameter(Position = 0)]
        [string] $Path,

        # Only run the tests that match this tag(s).
        [string[]] $Tag,

        # Exclude the tests that match this tag(s).
        [string[]] $ExcludeTag,

        # Only run the tests of these products: keys such as entra or exchange, or an alias such as 'Entra ID'.
        # Matches a test's Product or any of its RelatedProduct values. '*' wildcards are allowed.
        [string[]] $Product,

        # Do not run the tests of these products, matched like -Product. Wins over every selector.
        # A test without a product, such as a Pester-format custom test, is never excluded.
        [string[]] $ExcludeProduct,

        # Only run the tests about these features of a product, for example conditional-access. '*' wildcards are allowed.
        [string[]] $Feature,

        # Only run the tests of these security areas, for example authentication or privileged-access. '*' wildcards are allowed.
        [string[]] $Area,

        # Only run the tests with these severities: Critical, High, Medium, Low or Info.
        # A severity set for a test in the run configuration is the one that counts.
        [string[]] $Severity,

        # Only run the tests of these suites, for example Maester, CISA, CIS, ASD, EIDSCA, ORCA or AD. '*' wildcards are allowed.
        [string[]] $Suite,

        # Run these Maester Packs, by pack ID or code, for example ZTA or maester.zero-trust-assessment.
        # '*' wildcards are allowed. An installed pack runs only when it is named here (or turned on with
        # "Enabled": true in the config), so installing a pack never adds its tests to every run. A pack named
        # here runs even if it is off by default or in the config, and its long-running and preview tests run
        # too. Other packs do not run; the other tests are not affected.
        [string[]] $Pack,

        # Run every installed pack, as if each were named with -Pack, except those the config turns off.
        [switch] $AllPacks,

        # Include long running tests.
        [switch] $IncludeLongRunning,

        # Include preview tests.
        [switch] $IncludePreview,

        # The path to the file to save the test results in html format. The filename should include an .html extension.
        [string] $OutputHtmlFile,

        # Affected objects are collected by default. The switch is kept so that older scripts still run.
        [switch] $IncludeAffectedObjects,

        # Do not collect the affected objects: the consolidated list of objects the run touched.
        # By default the results carry the AffectedObjects property, the html report has an Affected objects page
        # when any test recorded an object and, with -OutputFolder, the <name>-affected-objects.json file is written
        # (plus -affected-objects.csv with -ExportCsv). Use this switch to keep the report smaller. The objects are
        # still collected when -RedactUserIdentity is used, since redaction is driven by them, but left out of the outputs.
        [switch] $ExcludeAffectedObjects,

        # Replaces user identities (display names, user principal names and object ids) with stable
        # stable ids in the generated outputs.
        # None (default): no redaction.
        # AllOutputs: redact every generated output (html, json, markdown, csv, Excel, affected objects json and csv).
        # HtmlOnly: redact the html report only, so the machine readable exports keep the
        # real identifiers for follow up while the shareable report does not.
        [ValidateSet('None', 'HtmlOnly', 'AllOutputs')]
        [string] $RedactUserIdentity = 'None',

        # The path to the file to save the test results in markdown format. The filename should include a .md extension.
        [string] $OutputMarkdownFile,

        # The path to the file to save a compact markdown summary with only result counters. The filename should include a .md extension.
        [string] $OutputMarkdownSummaryFile,

        # The path to the file to save the test results in json format. The filename should include a .json extension.
        [string] $OutputJsonFile,

        # The folder to save the test results in. If no -Output* is set, defaults to ./test-results.
        # If set, other -Output* parameters are ignored and all formats will be generated (markdown, markdown summary, html, json) with a timestamp and saved in the folder.
        [string] $OutputFolder,

        # The filename prefix to use for all the files in the output folder. e.g. 'TestResults' will generate TestResults.html, TestResults.md, TestResults.json.
        [string] $OutputFolderFileName,

        # An optional Pester configuration for Pester-format custom tests: a [PesterConfiguration] object or a
        # hashtable. Its Run.Path, Filter.Tag, Filter.ExcludeTag and TestResult options also apply to native tests.
        # Pester is needed only when the run has Pester-format tests.
        # See [Pester Configuration](https://pester.dev/docs/usage/Configuration) for more information.
        [object] $PesterConfiguration,

        # Set the Pester verbosity level. Default is 'None'.
        # None      : Shows only the final summary.
        # Normal    : Focus on successful containers and failed tests/blocks. Shows basic discovery information and the summary of all tests.
        # Detailed  : Similar to Normal, but this level shows all blocks and tests, including successful.
        # Diagnostic: Very verbose, but useful when troubleshooting tests. This level behaves like Detailed, but also enables debug messages.
        [ValidateSet('None', 'Normal', 'Detailed', 'Diagnostic')]
        [string] $Verbosity = 'None',

        # Run the tests in non-interactive mode. This will prevent the test results from being opened in the default browser and suppress all pretty messages.
        [switch] $NonInteractive,

        # Passes the output of the Maester tests to the console.
        [switch] $PassThru,

        # Optional: The email addresses of the report recipients. e.g. john@contoso.com
        # No email will be sent if this parameter is not provided.
        [string[]] $MailRecipient,

        # If sending the report to an email recipient, provide an absolute HTTP or HTTPS Uri to the detailed test results page.
        [ValidateScript({
                $uri = $null
                if ($_ -and -not ([Uri]::TryCreate($_, [UriKind]::Absolute, [ref]$uri) -and $uri.Scheme -in @('http', 'https'))) {
                    throw 'MailTestResultsUri must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URI, e.g. https://contoso.com/maester/report.html'
                }
                return $true
            })]
        [string] $MailTestResultsUri,

        # The user id of the sender of the mail. Defaults to the current user.
        # This is required when using application permissions.
        [string] $MailUserId,

        # Optional: The Teams team where the test results should be posted.
        # To get the TeamId, right-click on the channel in Teams and select 'Get link to channel'. Use the value of groupId. e.g. ?groupId=<TeamId>
        [string] $TeamId,

        # Optional: The channel where the results message should be posted. e.g. 19%3A00000000000000000000000000000000%40thread.tacv2
        # To get the TeamChannelId, right-click on the channel in Teams and select 'Get link to channel'. Use the value found between channel and the channel name. e.g. /channel/<TeamChannelId>/my%20channel
        [string] $TeamChannelId,

        # Optional: The webhook Uri where the results message should be posted. e.g. https://some-url/?value=123
        # To get the Webhook Uri, right-click on the channel in Teams and select 'Workflow'. Create a workflow using the 'Post to a channel when a webhook request is received' template. Use the value after 'complete.'
        [string] $TeamChannelWebhookUri,

        # Skip the graph connection check.
        # This is used for running tests that does not require a Graph connection.
        [switch] $SkipGraphConnect,

        # Do not send the run events to api.maester.dev: a random installation ID, a hash of the
        # tenant ID, the versions and platform, when the run started and how long it took, its outcome, the result
        # counts and the public packs installed and run.
        # Setting the environment variable MAESTER_DISABLE_TELEMETRY to 1 does the same for every command.
        [switch] $DisableTelemetry,

        # Skip the version check.
        # If set, the version check will not be performed.
        [switch] $SkipVersionCheck,

        # Export the results to a CSV file.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Export the results to a CSV file. Use with -OutputFolder to specify the folder.')]
        [switch] $ExportCsv,

        # Export the results to an Excel file.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Export the results to an Excel file. Use with -OutputFolder to specify the folder.')]
        [switch] $ExportExcel,

        # Do not show the Maester logo.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Do not show the logo when starting Maester.')]
        [switch] $NoLogo,

        # How the console output is written: Auto, Interactive, Stream or Plain.
        [ValidateSet('Auto', 'Interactive', 'Stream', 'Plain')]
        [string] $OutputMode = 'Auto',

        # The root directory for configuration drift tracking.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Specify drift root directory, see https://maester.dev/docs/tests/MT.1060')]
        [string] $DriftRoot,

        # Only run the tests with these IDs. Exact IDs or '*' wildcards, case-insensitive.
        # A test named by its exact ID runs even if it is a preview or long-running test.
        [string[]] $TestId,

        # Do not run the tests with these IDs. Exact IDs or '*' wildcards, case-insensitive. Wins over -TestId.
        [string[]] $ExcludeTestId,

function Get-MtTest {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Lists Maester native tests and their metadata without connecting to a tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Without -Path, returns the tests that ship with Maester (the catalog). With -Path, reads the native
    tests (Test.<ID>.ps1) in a file or folder and validates them; each object's Errors property lists
    every problem with its line, and IsValid is $false when there is one. No test code is run.

    .PARAMETER Id
    Only tests with these IDs: exact IDs or '*' wildcards.

    .PARAMETER Tag
    Only tests that any of these tags select: a tag the test carries or, for a test that ships with Maester,
    its ID or one of the tags it carried in Maester 2.x.

    .PARAMETER Product
    Only tests of these products: keys such as entra, or an alias such as 'Entra ID'. Matches a test's
    Product or any of its RelatedProduct values. '*' wildcards are allowed.

    .PARAMETER Feature
    Only tests about these features of a product, for example conditional-access.

    .PARAMETER Area
    Only tests of these security areas, for example authentication.

    .PARAMETER Severity
    Only tests with these severities: Critical, High, Medium, Low or Info.

    .PARAMETER Suite
    Only tests of these suites, for example Maester, CISA or AD.

    .PARAMETER Path
    A Test.<ID>.ps1 file or a folder of them to validate.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtTest -Product entra -Severity High | Format-Table Id, Title, Feature, Area

    Lists the built-in Entra ID tests of high severity. The values of one selector are alternatives; different
    selectors must all match.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtTest -Path ./Custom | Where-Object { -not $_.IsValid } | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Errors

    Shows every problem in the custom tests.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Get-MtTest
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Position = 0)]
        [string[]] $Id,

        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Tag,

        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Product,

        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Feature,

        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Area,

        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Severity,

        [Parameter()]
        [string[]] $Suite,

        [Parameter()]
        [string] $Path
    )

    Write-Verbose "Get-MtTest: Id=$($Id -join ', ') Tag=$($Tag -join ', ') Path=$Path"
    $tests = if ($Path) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { Write-Error "The path '$Path' does not exist."; return }
        $root = if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Container) { (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).Path } else { Split-Path (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Path).Path -Parent }
        @(Get-MtNativeTestInventory -Path $Path -Root $root)
    } else {
        @(Get-MtTestCatalog)
    }
    # The typed selectors, with the same matching as Invoke-Maester.
    $selection = Resolve-MtSelection -RunConfig ([pscustomobject]@{ Selection = [pscustomobject]@{} }) -Product $Product -Feature $Feature -Area $Area -Severity $Severity -Suite $Suite
    $selectorInUse = Test-MtSelectorInUse -Selection $selection
    foreach ($t in $tests) {
        if ($Id -and -not (Test-MtIdMatch -Id $t.Id -Pattern $Id)) { continue }
        if ($Tag) {
            # What -Tag matches in a run: the test's own tags and, for a built-in test, its ID and its 2.x tags.
            $selectionTags = Get-MtSelectionTag -Test $t
            if (-not (@($selectionTags.Own) + @($selectionTags.Legacy) | Where-Object { $tg = $_; $Tag | Where-Object { $tg -like $_ } })) { continue }
        }
        if ($selectorInUse -and (Test-MtSelectorMatch -Selection $selection -Product (@($t.Product) + @($t.RelatedProduct)) -Feature $t.Feature -Area $t.Area -Severity $t.Severity -Suite $t.Suite)) { continue }
        $copy = [ordered]@{}
        foreach ($p in $t.PSObject.Properties) { $copy[$p.Name] = $p.Value }
        $copy.IsValid = -not ($t.Errors -and $t.Errors.Count -gt 0)
        $copy.PSTypeName = 'Maester.Test'
        [pscustomobject]$copy
    }
}
﻿function Get-MtArgumentCompleterTable {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Lists the parameters whose values Maester completes with Tab: Command, Parameter, Kind, Values and Narrow.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Register-MtArgumentCompleter registers one completer for each row, and Get-MtArgumentCompletion looks the row
    up to know what to list. Kind names the values (Get-MtCompletionCandidate). Values are a command's own names
    for the Service kind. Narrow is false for a selector whose list does not depend on the other selectors on the
    line: -ExcludeProduct may leave out any product.

    Every Command must be an exported command with the Parameter; the unit tests check each row.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    $row = {
        param([string] $Command, [string] $Parameter, [string] $Kind, [string[]] $Values = @(), [bool] $Narrow = $true)
        [pscustomobject]@{ Command = $Command; Parameter = $Parameter; Kind = $Kind; Values = $Values; Narrow = $Narrow }
    }

    # The selectors of a run, and Get-MtTest, which selects the same way.
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Product' 'Product'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'ExcludeProduct' 'Product' -Narrow $false
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Feature' 'Feature'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Area' 'Area'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Severity' 'Severity'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Suite' 'Suite'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Tag' 'Tag'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'ExcludeTag' 'Tag'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'TestId' 'TestId'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'ExcludeTestId' 'TestId'
    & $row 'Invoke-Maester' 'Pack' 'Pack'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Id' 'TestId'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Tag' 'Tag'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Product' 'Product'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Feature' 'Feature'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Area' 'Area'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Severity' 'Severity'
    & $row 'Get-MtTest' 'Suite' 'Suite'
    & $row 'Invoke-MtTest' 'Id' 'TestId'

    # Writing a test: the keys the taxonomy allows, whatever tests exist.
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Product' 'TaxonomyProduct'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Feature' 'TaxonomyFeature'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Area' 'TaxonomyArea'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'ResourceType' 'ResourceType'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Mitre' 'Mitre'
    & $row 'New-MtTest' 'Service' 'TestService'

    # Packs: Invoke-Maester -Pack takes a code or an ID; the pack commands take IDs.
    & $row 'Get-MtPack' 'Id' 'PackId'
    & $row 'Restore-MtPack' 'Id' 'InstalledPackId'
    & $row 'Update-MtPack' 'Id' 'InstalledPackId'
    & $row 'Uninstall-MtPack' 'Id' 'InstalledPackId'

    # Connections: each command's own service names (as its Resolve-MtRequestedService call has them), then the
    # services of pack connectors.
    & $row 'Connect-Maester' 'Service' 'Service' @('ActiveDirectory', 'All', 'Azure', 'Dataverse', 'ExchangeOnline', 'GitHub', 'Graph', 'SecurityCompliance', 'Teams', 'SharePointOnline')
    & $row 'Test-MtConnection' 'Service' 'Service' @('ActiveDirectory', 'All', 'Azure', 'AzureDevOps', 'ExchangeOnline', 'EOP', 'GitHub', 'Graph', 'SecurityCompliance', 'SharePointOnline', 'Teams')
    & $row 'Get-MtConnector' 'Service' 'Service'

    & $row 'Get-MtSetting' 'Name' 'Setting'
    & $row 'Get-MtRoleMember' 'Role' 'Role'
}

﻿function ConvertTo-MtCompletionTest {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Keeps what Tab completion uses of test rows: the catalogue, a custom test inventory or a pack's test list.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Each row has Id, Title, Product, RelatedProduct, Feature, Area, Severity, Suite, Control (the references and
    the requirement IDs alone, so MS.AAD.3.1 finds the test mapped to cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1), Lifecycle,
    LongRunning, IsFamily, Tags (what -Tag matches, without the test's ID: its own tags, its suite's and, for a
    built-in test, its Maester 2.x tags), Source (BuiltIn, Custom or Pack), Pack, SortKey (the ID with its
    numbers padded, so MT.1005 sorts before MT.1010) and Candidate (filled in by Get-MtCompletionCandidate the
    first time the test is listed). Rows without an Id are dropped. One call takes all the rows, with plain
    loops: completion has to be fast.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Test,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [ValidateSet('BuiltIn', 'Custom', 'Pack')] [string] $Source,
        # The pack the rows come from.
        [Parameter()] [string] $Pack
    )

    $legacy = if ($Source -eq 'BuiltIn') { (Get-MtLegacyTagTable).ByTest } else { $null }
    foreach ($t in $Test) {
        if ($null -eq $t -or -not $t.Id) { continue }
        $id = [string]$t.Id
        $tags = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        foreach ($tag in @($t.Tag) + @($t.SuiteTag)) { if ($tag) { $null = $tags.Add([string]$tag) } }
        $old = $null
        if ($legacy -and $legacy.TryGetValue($id, [ref] $old)) { foreach ($tag in $old) { $null = $tags.Add([string]$tag) } }
        $control = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
        foreach ($reference in @($t.Control)) {
            if (-not $reference) { continue }
            $control.Add([string]$reference)
            $colon = ([string]$reference).IndexOf(':')
            if ($colon -gt 0) { $control.Add(([string]$reference).Substring($colon + 1)) }
        }
        $related = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
        foreach ($product in @($t.RelatedProduct)) { if ($product) { $related.Add([string]$product) } }
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id             = $id
            Title          = [string]$t.Title
            Product        = [string]$t.Product
            RelatedProduct = $related.ToArray()
            Feature        = [string]$t.Feature
            Area           = [string]$t.Area
            Severity       = [string]$t.Severity
            Suite          = [string]$t.Suite
            Control        = $control.ToArray()
            Lifecycle      = [string]$t.Lifecycle
            LongRunning    = [bool]$t.LongRunning
            IsFamily       = [bool]$t.InstanceSource
            Tags           = [string[]]@($tags)
            Source         = $Source
            Pack           = $Pack
            # Each number padded to 10 digits, with two plain replacements: a script block evaluator is slow.
            SortKey        = ($id -replace '\d+', '0000000000$0') -replace '(?<!\d)\d*(\d{10})(?!\d)', '$1'
            Candidate      = $null
        }
    }
}

﻿function Select-MtAffectedObjectByType {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Filters consolidated object records down to the types that count as an affected object.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Applies the catalog from Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition:
    - Types listed under ExcludedTypes are dropped silently (known findings, not objects).
    - For systems listed under KnownTypes, any other type is dropped and summarized in a
      warning so it can be triaged and added to the catalog.
    - Records of any other system pass through unchanged.

    .EXAMPLE
    Select-MtAffectedObjectByType -Objects $inventory

    Returns the inventory without Entra recommendations, PIM alerts and unknown types.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object[]])]
    param(
        # Consolidated object records to filter.
        [Parameter(Mandatory = $false)]
        [AllowEmptyCollection()]
        [object[]] $Objects
    )

    if (-not $Objects) { return @() }

    $definition = Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition
    $kept = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
    $dropped = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()

    foreach ($affectedObject in $Objects) {
        $system = [string]$affectedObject.System
        $type = [string]$affectedObject.Type

        if ($definition.ExcludedTypes.ContainsKey($system) -and $definition.ExcludedTypes[$system] -contains $type) {
            Write-Verbose "Affected objects: dropping excluded type $system/$type."
            continue
        }

        if ($definition.KnownTypes.ContainsKey($system) -and $definition.KnownTypes[$system] -notcontains $type) {
            $dropped.Add($affectedObject)
            continue
        }

        $kept.Add($affectedObject)
    }

    if ($dropped.Count -gt 0) {
        $summary = $dropped | Group-Object -Property { "$($_.System)/$($_.Type)" } |
            Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name) ($($_.Count))" }
        Write-Warning ("Affected objects: {0} record(s) of unknown type were dropped: {1}. Add the type to Get-MtAffectedObjectTypeDefinition (KnownTypes) to inventory it, or to ExcludedTypes if it is not an affected object." -f $dropped.Count, ($summary -join ', '))
    }

    return , $kept.ToArray()
}

153-
154-A fact can also carry a `Key` and a `Raw` value, for code that reads the results (a summary, an insight, another
155-report) and should not have to parse text such as `2026-06-15 (143 days ago)`. `Value` stays the text people read;
156-`Raw` is the same thing as data: a boolean, a number, a string, a list of strings, or a date (kept as ISO 8601 UTC
157-text). `Raw` is kept only with a `Key`, and a fact without a `Key` is shown the same way.
158-
159-```powershell
160-@{ Name = 'MFA'; Value = 'Not registered'; Tone = 'Risk'; Key = 'user.mfaRegistered'; Raw = $false }
161-```
162-
163-Use a key from this list when one fits, so the same fact means the same thing whichever source adds it. A key is
164-dotted camelCase; for a fact the list does not have, use a prefix of your own (`contoso.reviewDue`).
165-
166-| Key | Raw | Meaning |
167-| --- | --- | --- |
168-| `user.mfaRegistered` | boolean | The user has registered a method for multifactor authentication. |
169-| `user.passwordless` | boolean | The user can sign in without a password. |
170-| `user.privilegedRoles` | list of strings | The privileged Entra roles the user holds, permanent, activated or eligible. Empty when none. |
171-| `signIn.daysSince` | number, or null | Days between the last sign-in and when the data was read (`AsOf`). Null when no sign-in was recorded. Users, apps and devices. |
172-| `device.joinType` | string | `AzureAd` (Entra joined), `ServerAd` (hybrid joined) or `Workplace` (registered). |
173-| `device.managed` | boolean | The device is managed by Intune or another MDM. |
174-| `device.compliant` | boolean | The device meets its compliance policies. |

176-| `app.credentialExpired` | boolean | The app has at least one expired client secret or certificate. |
177-| `app.ownerCount` | number | How many owners the app registration (or agent identity blueprint) has. |
178-| `app.highPrivilegePermissions` | list of strings | The app's Tier 0 Microsoft Graph application permissions, those with a path to Global Administrator. Empty when none. |

content.content:
### Merge rules

- `TestSettings` rows merge per `Id` (case-insensitive) and per property: a higher layer can change one property
  of a row without repeating the others.
- Every other object merges per key, recursively.
- Arrays and plain values replace. An empty array in a higher layer clears the lower one.
- On the command line, `-Tag` and `-TestId` replace the config's `Selection.Tag` and `Selection.TestId`;
  `-ExcludeTag`, `-ExcludeTestId` and `-ExcludeProduct` add to the config's lists; `-IncludePreview` and
  `-IncludeLongRunning` turn the setting on when either source does.

Keys Maester does not know are kept and passed through, so they do no harm. The 2.x keys `ModuleVersion` and
`ConfigVersion` are ignored.

## A complete example

```json
{
  "Metadata": { "RunId": "2026-10-06-nightly", "RequestedBy": "security-pipeline" },
  "GlobalSettings": {
    "EmergencyAccessAccounts": [
      { "Type": "User", "UserPrincipalName": "BreakGlass1@contoso.com" },
      { "Type": "Group", "Id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" }
    ]
  },
  "Selection": {
    "BuiltIn": "All",
    "DefaultAction": "Run",
    "Product": [],
    "ExcludeProduct": [],
    "Feature": [],
    "Area": [],
    "Severity": [],
    "Suite": [],
    "Pack": [],
    "Tag": [],
    "ExcludeTag": [],
    "TestId": [],
    "ExcludeTestId": ["MT.1024.*"],
    "IncludePreview": false,
    "IncludeLongRunning": false,
    "OnUnknownId": "Warn"
  },
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "MT.1005", "Severity": "Critical" },
    { "Id": "MT.1089", "Enabled": false, "Reason": "Not relevant for this tenant" },
    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 }, "TimeoutSeconds": 600 }
  ],
  "Environment": {
    "TenantType": "Auto",
    "Cloud": "GCC",
    "Licenses": "Auto",
    "Services": "Auto",
    "Enforce": { "Service": true, "License": true, "TenantType": false, "Cloud": false }
  },
  "Execution": { "TestTimeoutSeconds": 0, "LongRunningTimeoutSeconds": 0 },
  "Output": {
    "ErrorsAsFailures": false,
    "TestResult": { "Format": "NUnitXml", "Path": "./test-results/maester.xml" }
  }
}
```

Every section is optional.

## Metadata

Free-form values about the run, echoed in the result as `RunMetadata`. Use it to tag a run, for example with a
`RunId` shared by the parts of a [split run](../result-schema.md#splitting-a-run-across-processes).

## GlobalSettings

Tenant-wide settings that tests read with `Get-MtSetting`. Maester knows these:

| Setting | Type | Default | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `EmergencyAccessAccounts` | array | none | Conditional Access checks. See [Emergency access accounts](./emergency-access-accounts.md). |
| `DataverseEnvironmentUrl` | string | | Copilot Studio checks. |
| `GitHubOrganization` | string | | GitHub checks. |
| `GitHubApiBaseUri` | string | `https://api.github.com` | GitHub checks. |
| `GitHubApiVersion` | string | `2022-11-28` | GitHub checks. |
| `XspmExternalDataUris` | object | built-in sources | XSPM checks. See the [overview](./overview.md#xspm-external-data-sources). |

Any other key is passed through. Custom tests and test packs should use a `Namespace.Key` name, for example
`Contoso.SiteUrl`.

## Selection

Which tests run. Every key has a command-line equivalent.

| Key | Values | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BuiltIn` | `All`, `None` | `All` | `None` runs only your custom tests, like `-SkipBuiltIn`. |
| `DefaultAction` | `Run`, `Skip` | `Run` | `Skip` is allow-list mode: a test runs only if a `TestSettings` row for its ID sets `"Enabled": true`. Others are `NotRun` with reason `NotListed`. |
| `Product` | array | `[]` | Run only tests of these products (like `-Product`): keys such as `entra` or `exchange`, or an alias such as `Entra ID`. Matches a test's `Product` or any of its `RelatedProduct` values. |
| `ExcludeProduct` | array | `[]` | Do not run tests of these products (like `-ExcludeProduct`), matched like `Product`. Wins over `Product`, `TestId` and the other selectors. A test with no product is never excluded. |
| `Feature` | array | `[]` | Run only tests about these features (like `-Feature`), for example `conditional-access`. |
| `Area` | array | `[]` | Run only tests of these security areas (like `-Area`), for example `authentication`. |
| `Severity` | array | `[]` | Run only tests with these severities (like `-Severity`). The severity a `TestSettings` row sets is the one that counts. |
| `Suite` | array | `[]` | Run only tests of these suites (like `-Suite`), for example `Maester`, `CISA`, `CIS`, `ASD`, `EIDSCA`, `ORCA` or `AD`. |
| `Pack` | array | `[]` | Run only these [Maester Packs](../packs/index.md#choosing-which-packs-run), by pack ID or code (like `-Pack`). A pack named here runs even if it is off, with its long-running and preview tests. Other packs do not run. |
| `Tag` | array | `[]` | Run only tests that any of these tags selects (like `-Tag`). |
| `ExcludeTag` | array | `[]` | Do not run tests that any of these tags selects (like `-ExcludeTag`). |
| `TestId` | array | `[]` | Run only these IDs (like `-TestId`). |
| `ExcludeTestId` | array | `[]` | Do not run these IDs (like `-ExcludeTestId`). Wins over `TestId`. |
| `IncludePreview` | bool | `false` | Run preview tests (like `-IncludePreview`). |
| `IncludeLongRunning` | bool | `false` | Run long-running tests (like `-IncludeLongRunning`). |
| `OnUnknownId` | `Warn`, `Ignore`, `Error` | `Warn` | What to do when an ID you named matches no test. `Error` stops the run before any test runs. |

Rules:

- `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `Severity` and `Suite` select by the attributes of a test. The values of one
  selector are alternatives, and different selectors must all match: `-Product entra, exchange -Severity High`
  runs the high-severity tests of either product. They combine the same way with `Tag` and `TestId`. Values are
  compared case-insensitively and `*` wildcards are allowed. The keys are listed in
  [`MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1),
  and each result names the ones it uses under `Taxonomy`.
- A Pester-format test has no product, feature or area, so a run that selects by one of them leaves it out. Its
  suite is that of its folder, and its severity counts only when a `TestSettings` row sets it.
- `ExcludeProduct` leaves out the tests whose `Product` or `RelatedProduct` matches, with the reason
  `ExcludedByProduct`: `-ExcludeProduct exchange` runs everything except the Exchange Online tests, and
  `-Product entra -ExcludeProduct entra` runs nothing. Unlike `Product`, it never leaves out a Pester-format
  test, which has no product. Services that only the excluded tests need are not read or connected.
- A command-line value replaces the list of the same name in the config, except `-ExcludeTag`,
  `-ExcludeTestId` and `-ExcludeProduct`, which add to it.
- Tags and IDs are compared case-insensitively. Tag lists match any tag; `*` wildcards are allowed.
- Test IDs are exact or use `*` wildcards (`CISA.MS.AAD.3.*`). An ID named exactly runs even if the test is
  preview or long-running; a wildcard match does not lift those exclusions.
- Preview tests (`Lifecycle = 'Preview'`) are left out unless `IncludePreview` is set or any `Tag` is given.
  Long-running tests are left out unless `IncludeLongRunning` is set or `Tag` contains `LongRunning` or
  `CAWhatIf`. Selecting by product, feature, area, severity or suite does not lift either exclusion.
- The tags `All` and `Full` were removed in 3.0 (in 2.x they were deprecated and selected nothing). Using
  them stops the run; use `IncludePreview` and `IncludeLongRunning` instead.
- Tests that need Active Directory run only after `Connect-Maester -Service ActiveDirectory`, whatever the
  selection says.
- In `DefaultAction: Skip` mode, a row with only `Severity` or `Parameters` does not admit a test, and admission
  is only the first gate: the selectors, tags and the preview and long-running rules still apply. A row on a
  family's parent ID or on any of its instance IDs admits the family. With no `"Enabled": true` rows at all,
  nothing runs.
- Unknown IDs are listed in the result under `Selection.UnknownIds`. An ID under a declared family's parent ID is
  never unknown, so you can keep a row for an instance that does not exist in this run.

### Tags

A tag selects a test that carries it in the `Tag` of its `[MaesterTest]` attribute, or whose folder's
`suite.json` lists it under `Tags`. Tags are for your own tests. The tests that ship with Maester no longer
carry tags for their suite, product, topic or severity, because each of those is an attribute.

The tags of Maester 2.x keep working. `-Tag CA`, `-Tag CIS`, `-ExcludeTag MS.AAD.3.5` and every other 2.x tag
select the built-in tests that carried the tag in 2.x, and the ID of a built-in test is still one of its tags,
so `-Tag MT.1068` selects it. A run that selects through a 2.x tag writes one warning that names the tag and,
where there is one, the selector that replaces it. Tests added after Maester 3.0 do not carry 2.x tags, so move
to the selectors when you can:

| 2.x tag | Example | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Suite | `CISA`, `Maester` | `-Suite cisa` |
| Product or service | `EXO`, `Entra` | `-Product exchange`; `-ExcludeTag EXO` is `-ExcludeProduct exchange` |
| Topic | `CA`, `Privileged` | `-Feature conditional-access`, `-Area privileged-access` |
| Benchmark control ID | `MS.AAD.3.5` | `-TestId CISA.MS.AAD.3.5` |
| Severity | `Severity:High` | `-Severity High` |
| A test's ID | `MT.1068` | `-TestId MT.1068` |

The 2.x tags and the test ID are used for selection only. A result row's `Tag` lists the tags written in the
test, and its `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `Suite` and `Severity` fields say the rest.

Deselected and disabled tests still appear in the result as `NotRun` rows with a reason code. See
[Applicability and reason codes](./applicability.md).

## TestSettings

One row per test you want to change, built-in or custom, native or Pester-format.

| Key | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Id` | string | The test ID, or a family instance ID (`MT.1024.<suffix>`). Required. |
| `Severity` | string | `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low` or `Info`. Overrides the test's own severity. |
| `Enabled` | bool | `false` turns the test off: it is not run and appears as `NotRun` with reason `DisabledByConfig`. `true` admits it in `DefaultAction: Skip` mode. |
| `Reason` | string | Shown as the reason of a disabled test. |
| `Parameters` | object | Values for the test's parameters, by name. Native tests only. |
| `TimeoutSeconds` | int | A timeout for this test, overriding `Execution`. Native tests only. |

For a family, a row on an instance ID wins over a row on the parent ID. `"Enabled": false` on the parent ID turns off the whole family; on an instance ID it
turns off only that instance, and the others still run. `Parameters` and `TimeoutSeconds` on an instance ID apply to
that instance only: a parameter the instance row does not name keeps the value of the family's row, and
`"TimeoutSeconds": 0` turns the timeout off for that instance.

Parameter values are checked against the test's `param()` block before it runs. Use `Get-MtTest <ID>` to see a
test's parameters, their types, defaults, allowed values and descriptions.

| Parameter type | Accepted JSON value |
| --- | --- |
| `int` | A whole number in the 32-bit range |
| `bool`, `switch` | `true` or `false` |
| `string` | A string, or `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }` (the test receives the `Id`) |
| `string[]` | A string or an array of strings (or of `{ "Id": ... }` objects) |

A name the test does not have, a fraction, a value of the wrong type, a value outside the parameter's
`ValidateRange` or `ValidateSet`, a value that does not match its [kind](../writing-tests/index.mdx#parameter-kinds),
a common parameter name, or an engine-owned name (`Instance`, `Mt*`) gives that test an `Error` row with reason

﻿function Convert-MtResultsToFlatObject {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Convert Maester test results to a flattened object that can be exported to CSV or Excel.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Convert Maester test results to a flattened object that can be exported to CSV or Excel. This function exports
    the data to a CSV file by default, but can also export to an Excel file if the ImportExcel module is installed.

    The function also supports reading Maester test results from a JSON file and exporting the flattened object to a CSV.

    .PARAMETER InputObject
    Use the Maester test results from the pipeline or as an input object (JSON).

    .PARAMETER JsonFilePath
    The path of the file containing the Maester test results in JSON format.

    .PARAMETER ExportCsv
    Export the flattened object to a CSV file.

    .PARAMETER CsvFilePath
    The path of the file to export CSV data to.

    .PARAMETER ExportExcel
    Export the flattened object to an Excel workbook using the ImportExcel module.

    .PARAMETER ExcelFilePath
    The path of the file to export an Excel worksheet to.

    .PARAMETER Force
    Force the export to a CSV/XLSX file even if the file already exists.

    .PARAMETER PassThru
    Return the flattened object to the pipeline.

    .EXAMPLE
    Convert-MtResultsToFlatObject -JsonFilePath 'C:\path\to\results.json'

    Convert the Maester test results in C:\path\to\results.json to a flattened object that is then returned to the pipeline.

    .EXAMPLE
    Convert-MtResultsToFlatObject -JsonFilePath 'C:\path\to\results.json' -ExportExcel

    Convert the Maester test results in C:\path\to\results.json to a flattened object, and then export that object to an Excel file (C:\path\to\results.xlsx). Requires the ImportExcel module.

    .EXAMPLE
    Convert-MtResultsToFlatObject -JsonFilePath 'C:\path\to\results.json' -ExportCsv -CsvFilePath 'C:\path\to\results.csv'

    Convert the Maester test results in C:\path\to\results.json to a flattened object, and then export that object to C:\path\to\results.csv.

    .OUTPUTS
    System.Collections.Generic.List[PSObject]

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Convert-MtResultsToFlatObject

    .NOTES
    Due to limitations in CSV files and Excel cells, the ResultDetails property is limited to 30000 characters. If the
    test result details are longer than this, that section will be truncated and a notification will be included in its
    place. This is most likely to happen when details about a large number of users is included in the result details.
    The full details are still available in the JSON file and the HTML report.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(DefaultParameterSetName = 'FromFile')]
    [OutputType([System.Collections.Generic.List[PSObject]])]
    param (
        # The Maester test results passed from the pipeline using `Invoke-Maester -PassThru` or as an input object.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0, ValueFromPipeline, ParameterSetName = 'FromInputObject')]
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0, ValueFromPipeline, ParameterSetName = 'CSV')]
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0, ValueFromPipeline, ParameterSetName = 'XLSX')]
        [Alias('MaesterResults')]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [psobject] $InputObject,

        # The path to the JSON file containing the Maester test results.
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0, HelpMessage = 'The path to the JSON file containing the Maester test results.', ParameterSetName = 'FromFile')]
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0, HelpMessage = 'The path to the JSON file containing the Maester test results.', ParameterSetName = 'CSV')]
        [Parameter(Mandatory, Position = 0, HelpMessage = 'The path to the JSON file containing the Maester test results.', ParameterSetName = 'XLSX')]
        [ValidateScript({ Test-Path -Path $_ -PathType Leaf })]
        [string] $JsonFilePath,

        # Export the results to a CSV file.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Export the results to a CSV file.')]
        [switch] $ExportCsv,

        # Export the results to an Excel file.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Export the results to an Excel file.')]
        [switch] $ExportExcel,

        # The path to the CSV file to which the Maester test results will be exported.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Optional when JsonFilePath is provided. The path to the CSV file to which the Maester test results will be exported.', ParameterSetName = 'CSV')]
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Optional when JsonFilePath is provided. The path to the CSV file to which the Maester test results will be exported.', ParameterSetName = 'FromInputObject')]
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Optional when JsonFilePath is provided. The path to the CSV file to which the Maester test results will be exported.', ParameterSetName = 'FromFile')]
        [string] $CsvFilePath = "$($JsonFilePath -replace '\.json$', '.csv')",

        # The path to the Excel file to which the Maester test results will be exported.
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Optional when JsonFilePath is provided. The path to the Excel file to which the Maester test results will be exported.', ParameterSetName = 'XLSX')]
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Optional when JsonFilePath is provided. The path to the Excel file to which the Maester test results will be exported.', ParameterSetName = 'FromInputObject')]
        [Parameter(HelpMessage = 'Optional when JsonFilePath is provided. The path to the Excel file to which the Maester test results will be exported.', ParameterSetName = 'FromFile')]
        [string]$ExcelFilePath = "$($JsonFilePath -replace '\.json$', '.xlsx')",

        # Force the export to a CSV/XLSX file even if the file already exists.
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'FromInputObject', HelpMessage = 'Force the export to a CSV/XLSX file even if the file already exists.')]
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'FromFile', HelpMessage = 'Force the export to a CSV/XLSX file even if the file already exists.')]
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'CSV', HelpMessage = 'Force the export to a CSV file even if the file already exists.')]
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'XLSX', HelpMessage = 'Force the export to an Excel file even if the file already exists.')]
        [switch]
        $Force,

        # Return the flattened object to the pipeline.
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'FromInputObject', HelpMessage = 'Return the flattened object to the pipeline.')]
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'FromFile', HelpMessage = 'Return the flattened object to the pipeline.')]
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'CSV', HelpMessage = 'Return the flattened object to the pipeline.')]
        [Parameter(ParameterSetName = 'XLSX', HelpMessage = 'Return the flattened object to the pipeline.')]
        [switch]
        $PassThru
    )

    begin {

        # Check for an existing CSV file with the same name.
        if ( ($PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('CsvFilePath') -or $ExportCsv.IsPresent ) -and (Test-Path -Path $CsvFilePath -PathType Leaf) -and -not $Force.IsPresent) {
            throw "The specified CSV file path '$CsvFilePath' already exists. Use -Force if you want to overwrite this file or specify a new filename."
        }

        # Check for an existing Excel file with the same name.
        if ( ($PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('ExcelFilePath') -or $ExportExcel.IsPresent ) -and (Test-Path -Path $ExcelFilePath -PathType Leaf) -and -not $Force.IsPresent) {
            throw "The specified Excel file path '$ExcelFilePath' already exists. Use -Force if you want to overwrite this file or specify a new filename."
        }

        [string]$TruncationFYI = 'NOTE: DETAILS ARE TRUNCATED DUE TO FIELD SIZE LIMITATIONS. PLEASE SEE THE HTML REPORT FOR FULL DETAILS.'

        if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'FromInputObject') {
            $JsonData = $InputObject.Tests
        }

        if ($PSCmdlet.ParameterSetName -eq 'FromFile') {
            $JsonData = (Get-Content -Path $JsonFilePath | ConvertFrom-Json).Tests
        }

        $FlattenedResults = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[PSObject]

    } #end begin

    process {
        $JsonData | ForEach-Object {

            # Truncate the ResultDetail.TestResult data if it is longer than 30000 characters.
            if ($_.ResultDetail.TestResult.Length -gt 30000) {
                Write-Warning -Message "Truncating the ResultDetail.TestResult data for test '$($_.Name)' to 30000 characters."
                $TestResultDetail = "$TruncationFYI`n`n$($_.ResultDetail.TestResult -replace '(?s)(.*?)#### Impacted resources.*?#### Remediation actions:','$1#### Remediation actions:')"
                # Removing the impacted resources section is not enough when the detail has no such section.
                if ($TestResultDetail.Length -gt 30000) {
                    $TestResultDetail = $TestResultDetail.Substring(0, 30000)
                }
            } else {
                $TestResultDetail = $_.ResultDetail.TestResult
            }

            # Add the flattened object to the FlattenedResults list.
            $FlattenedResults.Add([PSCustomObject]@{
                    ID             = $_.ID
                    Title          = $_.Title
                    Result         = $_.Result
                    Severity       = $_.Severity
                    Tag            = $_.Tag -join ', '
                    Block          = $_.Block
                    Duration       = $_.Duration
                    Description    = $_.ResultDetail.TestDescription
                    ResultDetail   = $TestResultDetail
                    TestSkipped    = $_.ResultDetail.TestSkipped
                    SkippedReason  = $_.ResultDetail.SkippedReason
                    ErrorMessage   = $_.ErrorRecord.Exception.Message
                    Name           = $_.Name
                    HelpUrl        = $_.HelpUrl
                    TestScriptFile = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($_.ScriptBlockFile)
                })
        }

        # Export the FlattenedResults list to a CSV if requested.
        if ($ExportCsv.IsPresent -or $PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey('CsvFilePath')) {

            # Warn if the specified file path ends with the wrong extension.
            if ($CsvFilePath -match '\.xlsx$') {
                Write-Output ''
                Write-Warning -Message 'You are exporting a CSV file, but the file path ends with the .XLSX extension. Please rename with the proper extension or use the ''-ExcelFilePath'' parameter if you want an Excel file.' -WarningAction Continue
            }

            try {
                if ($PSVersionTable.PSVersion.Major -ge 6) {
                    $FlattenedResults | Export-Csv -Path $CsvFilePath -UseQuotes Always -Encoding utf8BOM -NoTypeInformation
                } else {
                    # Windows PowerShell has no -UseQuotes (it always quotes) and its UTF8 encoding already writes a BOM.
                    $FlattenedResults | Export-Csv -Path $CsvFilePath -Encoding UTF8 -NoTypeInformation
                }
                Write-Verbose "Exported the Maester test results to '$CsvFilePath'." -InformationAction Continue
            } catch {
                Write-Error "Failed to export the Maester test results to a CSV file. $_"
            }
        }

The Maester test results returned from `Invoke-Pester -PassThru | ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult` [Parameter(Mandatory = $true, Position = 0)] [psobject] $MaesterResults ) $StatusIcon = @{ Passed = '' Failed = '' NotRun = '' Skipped = '' Investigate = '' Error = '' } $StatusIconSm = @{ Passed = '✅' Failed = '❌' NotRun = '❔' Skipped = '🚫' Investigate = '🔍' Error = '⚠️' } $ResultDisplayName = @{ Passed = 'Passed' Failed = 'Failed' NotRun = 'Not Run' Skipped = 'Skipped' Investigate = 'Investigate' Error = 'Error' } $SeverityIcon = @{ Critical = '🔴 Critical' High = '🟠 High' Medium = '🟡 Medium' Low = '🟢 Low' Info = 'ℹ️ Info' } function GetSeverityText($severity) { if ($severity -and $SeverityIcon.ContainsKey($severity)) { return $SeverityIcon[$severity] } else { return $severity } } # The report is several MB for a full run: build it with a StringBuilder, because appending to a string # with += copies the whole string each time. function GetTestSummary() { $summary = [System.Text.StringBuilder]::new(@' |Test|Severity|Status| |-|:-:|:-:| '@) foreach ($test in $MaesterResults.Tests) { $severityText = GetSeverityText $test.Severity [void]$summary.Append("| $($test.Name) | $severityText | $($StatusIcon[$test.Result]) |`n") } return $summary.ToString() } function GetTestDetails() { $details = [System.Text.StringBuilder]::new() foreach ($test in $MaesterResults.Tests) { [void]$details.Append("### $($StatusIconSm[$test.Result]) $($test.Name)`n`n") $severityText = GetSeverityText $test.Severity $resultName = if ($ResultDisplayName.ContainsKey($test.Result)) { $ResultDisplayName[$test.Result] } else { $test.Result } [void]$details.Append("**Severity:** $severityText      **Status:** $($StatusIconSm[$test.Result]) $resultName`n`n") if (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.ResultDetail)) { # Test author has provided details [void]$details.Append("#### Overview`n`n$($test.ResultDetail.TestDescription)`n`n") [void]$details.Append("#### Test Results`n`n$($test.ResultDetail.TestResult)`n`n") } elseif (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.ScriptBlock)) { # Test author has not provided details, use default code in script # make sure we do not execute the code in the script block! $cleanedScriptBlock = $test.ScriptBlock.ToString() -replace '%\w+%', '' -replace '\$_', '€_' # or show me how I can make it not execute the $_ thing [void]$details.Append("#### Overview`n`n``````ps1`n$cleanedScriptBlock`n```````n`n") if (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.ErrorRecord)) { [void]$details.Append("#### Reason for failure`n`n$($test.ErrorRecord)`n`n") } } if (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.HelpUrl)) { [void]$details.Append("**Learn more**: [$($test.HelpUrl)]($($test.HelpUrl))`n`n") } if (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.Tag)) { $tags = '`{0}`' -f ($test.Tag -join '` `') [void]$details.Append("**Tag**: $tags`n`n") } if (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.Block)) { $category = '`{0}`' -f ($test.Block -join '` `') [void]$details.Append("**Category**: $category`n`n") } if (![string]::IsNullOrEmpty($test.ScriptBlockFile)) { [void]$details.Append("**Source**: ``$($test.ScriptBlockFile)```n`n") } [void]$details.Append("---`n`n") } return $details.ToString() } $markdownFilePath = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '../../assets/ReportTemplate.md' $templateMarkdown = Get-Content -Path $markdownFilePath -Raw # Execute functions first so they don't mess with the markdown template $textSummary = GetTestSummary $textDetails = GetTestDetails $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TenandId%', $MaesterResults.TenantId $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TenantName%', $MaesterResults.TenantName $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TenantName%', $MaesterResults.TenantVersion $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%ModuleVersion%', $MaesterResults.CurrentVersion $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TestDate%', $MaesterResults.ExecutedAt $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TotalCount%', $MaesterResults.TotalCount $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%PassedCount%', $MaesterResults.PassedCount $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%FailedCount%', $MaesterResults.FailedCount $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%InvestigateCount%', $MaesterResults.InvestigateCount $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%SkippedCount%', $MaesterResults.SkippedCount $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%NotRunCount%', $MaesterResults.NotRunCount $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TestSummary%', $textSummary $templateMarkdown = $templateMarkdown -replace '%TestDetails%', $textDetails return $templateMarkdown } ﻿# Maester Test Results This is a summary of the test results from the Maester test run. **Tenant:** %TenantName% **Date:** %TestDate% | 🔥
