---
title: Result schema
description: Reference for the Maester 3.0 result JSON (schema 2.1), the NUnit and JUnit XML files, and merging the results of a run split across processes.
sidebar:
  label: Result schema
---

# Result schema

`Invoke-Maester -PassThru` returns the result object, and `-OutputFolder` or `-OutputJsonFile` writes the same
object as JSON. Maester 3.0 keeps the 2.x shape: every 2.x field is still there with the same name, and the new
fields are additions. The result says which shape it has with `SchemaVersion = "2.1"`, meaning "the 2.x shape
plus the additions on this page". A reader written for 2.x keeps working.

Two 2.x fields have other values for the tests that ship with Maester, because those tests are now described by
typed attributes instead of a category and tags: `Block` is the name of the test's product, and `Tag` no longer
lists suite, product or benchmark tags or the test ID. See [Test rows](#test-rows).

## Top level

The 2.x fields are unchanged: `Result`, `FailedCount`, `PassedCount`, `ErrorCount`, `InvestigateCount`,
`SkippedCount`, `NotRunCount`, `TotalCount`, `ExecutedAt`, `TotalDuration`, `UserDuration`,
`DiscoveryDuration`, `FrameworkDuration`, `TenantId`, `TenantName`, `TenantLogos`, `Account`,
`CurrentVersion`, `LatestVersion`, `SystemInfo`, `PowerShellInfo`, `LoadedModules`, `InvokeCommand`,
`MgContext`, `PesterConfig`, `MaesterConfig`, `Tests`, `Blocks` and `EndOfJson` (always last). `OutputFiles` and
`AffectedObjects` appear when requested, as before.

Added in 2.1:

| Field | Type | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SchemaVersion` | string | `"2.1"`. |
| `CatalogVersion` | string | The version of the built-in test catalog, equal to the module version. Results are comparable when this matches. |
| `TenantContext` | object | The facts the run used to decide which tests apply (below). |
| `Taxonomy` | object | The display names of the product, feature, area and resource type keys and of the ATT&CK techniques that the rows use (below). |
| `RunMetadata` | object | The `Metadata` section of the run configuration, echoed as given (for example a run ID). An empty object when not set. |
| `Selection` | object | How the run selected tests (below). |
| `Frameworks` | array | The catalogue of each framework the rows map to, so a report can show the requirements no test checks (below). Empty when no row names a framework. |
| `Packs` | array | The [Maester Packs](./packs/index.md) of the run, including packs that could not run (below). Only present when the run had packs. |
| `Previous` | object | The results of the last run on the same tenant in the output folder, so a report can show what changed (below). Only present when `Invoke-Maester` found one. |

function Get-MtStepProblem {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns one message for each thing that is wrong with the step catalogue or with the steps that tests name.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Used by the catalog build, which fails on any message, and by the unit tests (docs/proposals/defenders-path.md,
    section 14). It returns:

    - the problems of the catalogue itself (Get-MtStepCatalog) and of the measure registry (Get-MtMeasureRegistry);
    - a step whose Measure names a key the registry does not have, and a registry entry whose reader function the
      module does not have;
    - a test whose Step names a step the catalogue does not have;
    - with -Coverage, when -Test is every built-in test: a step that no test names and that has no Measure but has
      no Unchecked reason, and a step that a test names but still has one;
    - too many sources that cite a maintainer instead of Microsoft Learn (more than one in ten).

    The build checks a test folder that may hold only some of the tests (a fixture, in the unit tests), so it leaves
    out -Coverage; the unit tests pass it with the full set.

    A pack's tests name steps in its taxonomy.json (packs/<name>/taxonomy.json, Tests.<id>.Step), which -PackRoot
    reads. Each message starts with the path of a file and names the step or the test.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([string])]
    param(
        # The built-in tests (Get-MtNativeTestInventory).
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Test,

        [Parameter()] [string] $PackRoot,

        [Parameter()] [object] $Catalog = (Get-MtStepCatalog),

        # The measure registry the catalogue's Measure keys refer to. Defaults to the module's.
        [Parameter()] [object] $Registry = (Get-MtMeasureRegistry),

        # -Test is every built-in test: check that each step is named by a test or says in Unchecked why not.
        [Parameter()] [switch] $Coverage

84	    Feature or Area, is left out of a run that selects by one of them.
85	
86	    Returns an object with Selector (the name) and Value (the selector's values), or nothing when the test

91	    param(
92	        # Output of Resolve-MtSelection.

95	        [Parameter()] [AllowNull()] [AllowEmptyString()] [string] $Feature,

107	        foreach ($value in @($values[$name] | Where-Object { $_ })) {
108	            foreach ($pattern in $patterns) { if ($value -like $pattern) { $matched = $true; break } }

rep('powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare.ps1', [
["""    Returns an object with Count (compliant devices), Total (devices that signed in) and Objects (the devices that
    aren't compliant, as Type, Id and DisplayName).
""", """    Returns an object with Count (compliant devices), Total (devices that signed in) and Objects (the devices that
    aren't compliant, as Type, Id and DisplayName).

    For each device it lists, it adds the object facts device.managed, device.compliant, device.os and device.joinType
    (design section 12) with Add-MtAffectedObjectFact, from the source 'Maester measures'. The engine puts the
    objects of a measure on the Affected objects page, so the facts have an object to attach to. A run that doesn't
    collect affected objects keeps no facts.
"""],
["""        # isManaged, operatingSystem and trustType are read for the object facts device.managed, device.os and
        # device.joinType (design section 12). They wait for the engine to list a measure's objects on the Affected
        # objects page: facts attach only to objects the run lists.
""", """        # isManaged, operatingSystem and trustType are read for the object facts device.managed, device.os and
        # device.joinType (design section 12).
"""],
["""    $notCompliant = @($devices | Where-Object { $_.isCompliant -ne $true })
""", """    $notCompliant = @($devices | Where-Object { $_.isCompliant -ne $true })

    # Object facts for the devices listed, with the shared keys.
    $joinTypes = @{ AzureAd = 'Microsoft Entra joined'; ServerAd = 'Microsoft Entra hybrid joined'; Workplace = 'Microsoft Entra registered' }
    $facts = foreach ($device in $notCompliant) {
        if (-not $device.id) { continue }
        $managed = $device.isManaged -eq $true
        $list = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
        $list.Add(@{ Name = 'Management'; Value = $(if ($managed) { 'Managed' } else { 'Not managed' }); Tone = $(if ($managed) { 'Info' } else { 'Warning' }); Key = 'device.managed'; Raw = $managed })
        $list.Add(@{ Name = 'Compliance'; Value = 'Not compliant'; Tone = 'Warning'; Key = 'device.compliant'; Raw = $false })
        if ($device.operatingSystem) { $list.Add(@{ Name = 'Operating system'; Value = [string]$device.operatingSystem; Key = 'device.os'; Raw = [string]$device.operatingSystem }) }
        $trust = [string]$device.trustType
        if ($trust) { $list.Add(@{ Name = 'Join type'; Value = $(if ($joinTypes.ContainsKey($trust)) { $joinTypes[$trust] } else { $trust }); Key = 'device.joinType'; Raw = $trust }) }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Type = 'Device'; Id = [string]$device.id; Fact = $list.ToArray() }
    }
    if (@($facts).Count -gt 0) { $facts | Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Source 'Maester measures' }
"""],
])

rep('powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtMfaCapableShare.ps1', [
["""    Returns an object with Count (users who can complete MFA), Total (the users counted) and Objects (the users who
    can't, as Type, Id and DisplayName, administrators first).
""", """    Returns an object with Count (users who can complete MFA), Total (the users counted) and Objects (the users who
    can't, as Type, Id and DisplayName, administrators first).

    For each user it lists, it adds the object facts user.mfaCapable and user.mfaRegistered (design section 12) with
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact, from the source 'Maester measures', under the object ID and the user principal name,
    so a record has them whichever way it was keyed. A run that doesn't collect affected objects keeps no facts.
"""],
["""    # Object facts for these users (design section 12), under the object ID and the UPN, wait for the engine to list
    # a measure's objects on the Affected objects page: facts attach only to objects the run lists.
    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{""", """    # Object facts for the users listed (design section 12), under the object ID and the UPN.
    $facts = foreach ($user in $notCapable) {
        $list = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
        $list.Add(@{ Name = 'Can complete MFA'; Value = 'No: no method the policy allows is registered'; Tone = $(if ($user.isAdmin -eq $true) { 'Risk' } else { 'Warning' }); Key = 'user.mfaCapable'; Raw = $false })
        if ($null -ne $user.isMfaRegistered) {
            $registered = $user.isMfaRegistered -eq $true
            $list.Add(@{ Name = 'MFA'; Value = $(if ($registered) { 'Registered' } else { 'Not registered' }); Tone = $(if ($registered) { 'Info' } else { 'Warning' }); Key = 'user.mfaRegistered'; Raw = $registered })
        }
        $fact = $list.ToArray()
        [pscustomobject]@{ Type = 'User'; Id = [string]$user.id; Fact = $fact }
        if ($user.userPrincipalName) { [pscustomobject]@{ Type = 'User'; Id = [string]$user.userPrincipalName; Fact = $fact } }
    }
    if (@($facts).Count -gt 0) { $facts | Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Source 'Maester measures' }

    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{"""],
])

content.content:
| `Previous` | object | The results of the last run on the same tenant in the output folder, so a report can show what changed (below). Only present when `Invoke-Maester` found one. |
| `Partitions` | array | Only in a result merged with `Merge-MtMaesterResult -SameRun` (see [Splitting a run](#splitting-a-run-across-processes)). |

### TenantContext

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `TenantId`, `TenantName` | From the Graph connection. |
| `TenantType`, `TenantTypeSource` | `Workforce`, `External` or `Unknown`; source `Detected`, `Config` or `Unknown`. |
| `Cloud`, `CloudSource` | `Commercial`, `GCC`, `GCCHigh`, `DoD`, `China`, ... or `Unknown`; source `Detected`, `Assumed` (Commercial, which cannot be told apart from GCC), `Config` or `Unknown`. |
| `Platform` | `Windows`, `Linux` or `MacOS`. |
| `Services` | One property per service the run's tests need, `true` when connected. |
| `Licenses` | `State` (`Known` or `Unknown`), `ServicePlanNames`, `ServicePlanIds`, `SkuIds`, `Source` (`Detected`, `Config` or `Unknown`). |
| `AuthType`, `Account`, `Scopes` | From the Graph connection. |

### Taxonomy
A pack that the configuration turns off is not listed.

### Previous

```json
"Previous": { "ExecutedAt": "2026-10-26T09:12:40.0000000+11:00", "File": "TestResults-2026-10-26-091240.json",
              "Results": { "CIS.M365.1.1.1": "Passed", "MT.1001": "Failed" },
              "History": [ { "ExecutedAt": "2026-10-26T09:12:40.0000000+11:00", "Total": 453, "Passed": 141, "Failed": 98,
                             "Investigate": 18, "Error": 2, "Skipped": 175, "NotRun": 19 } ] }
```

`Invoke-Maester` reads the newest `TestResults-*.json` in the output folder that is for the same tenant, before
it writes this run's files, and keeps only each test's ID and result. A test that is in this result and not in
`Results` did not exist or did not run then. `History` holds the counts of up to ten earlier runs on the tenant,
newest first, read from the start of each file, so the report can draw a trend. `Compare-MtTestResult` compares two whole results. A result merged with
`Merge-MtMaesterResult -SameRun` has no `Previous`, because a part's previous file may be another part of an
earlier run; its `Frameworks` and `Packs` cover every part.

### MaesterConfig

`MaesterConfig` is the effective run configuration after every layer was merged (see
| `Feature` | string | The key of the part of the product the test is about, for example `conditional-access`. `Taxonomy.Features` gives the name. |
| `Area` | string | The key of the security theme, for example `authentication`. `Taxonomy.Areas` gives the name. |
| `ResourceType` | string | What a failing result points at, for example `Tenant` or `User`. |
| `UserImpact` | string | `Low`, `Medium` or `High`: how much the recommended fix disrupts end users. |
| `ImplementationCost` | string | `Low`, `Medium` or `High`: how much administrator work the recommended fix takes. |
| `Mitre` | array of strings | MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs the checked control prevents or detects, or the single value `None`. `Taxonomy.Attack` gives the names and tactics. |
| `Control` | array of strings | Framework requirements the test supports, written `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`: the values of the test's `Control` attribute, then the controls related to the requirements they name. See [Benchmark](#benchmark). |
| `Lifecycle` | string | `Preview`, `Stable` or `Deprecated`. `Stable` when the test does not say. |
| `ReplacedBy` | string | For a `Deprecated` test, the ID of the test that took its place. |
| `Service` | array of strings | The services the test needs, by their names in the service registry. |
| `License` | array of strings | The service plans the test needs; the tenant needs any one. |
| `Permission` | array of strings | The permissions the test declares, each written `<Service>:<Kind>:<Name>`. The test needs every element; `\|` inside an element joins alternatives, any one of which is enough. Recorded; not enforced. |
| `Benchmark` | object | The requirement of a published benchmark that the test implements: the first value of its `Control` attribute that a framework file knows. `null` when there is none. See [Benchmark](#benchmark). |
| `Format` | string | `Native` or `Pester`. |
| `ReasonCode` | string | Why the test did not run or did not produce a verdict. Empty for `Passed`, `Failed` and `Investigate`. See [Applicability and reason codes](./configuration/applicability.md#reason-codes). |
| `ReasonDetail` | string | The reason in words. For `TestError`, the first line of the error. |
| `ParentId` | string | For a family's rows, the family's ID. Also set on the single row that stands for a whole family that did not run. |
| `InstanceId` | string | For an instance row, its full ID (the same as `Id`). |
| `Parameters` | array | Native tests: the effective parameter values, each `{ Name, Value, Source, Kind }`, where `Source` is `Default`, `Config` or `Parameter`. Empty for Pester rows. |
| `Diagnostics` | array of strings | Warnings (`WARNING: ...`) and non-terminating errors (`ERROR: ...`) the test wrote. |
| `Package` | object | For a test from a [Maester Pack](./packs/index.md): `Id`, `Name`, `Version`, `Commit`, `Publisher`, `BuiltIn` and `Runtime` of the pack. `null` for every other test. A pack's rows always have `Source` `Custom`. |
| `Fields` | object | For an instance row, the `Fields` its family's instance source gave, for example `{ "Pillar": ["Identity"], "Category": "Access control" }` for a Zero Trust Assessment result. Values are strings or arrays of strings. `null` for every other row. |
| `ShimOf` | string | For a benchmark test whose body returns another built-in test (a shim), the ID of that test: both rows report the same setting. `null` for every other row. |

The fields from `Product` to `Permission` are the test's attributes; see
[the `[MaesterTest]` attribute](./writing-tests/index.mdx#the-maestertest-attribute). A native row always has
all of them: one the test does not declare is `null`, or `[]` for an array. A Pester-format row has them too,
all `null`.

A consumer that tracks results over time should key family rows on `ParentId` when it is present: a family that
did not run is one row on the parent ID, which 2.x never produced.

### Steps and Goals

The defender's path is the order a defender works in: what has to be in place before a fix works, and whether
the tenant is ready for it. A test names the steps it verifies with its `Step` attribute, and the step catalogue
that ships with Maester (`powershell/assets/steps/`) holds how steps relate and the Microsoft Learn pages behind
them. A step is in scope when a row that ran names it, or when it is a prerequisite, at any depth, of such a step.
The report, the console, CSV and Markdown read these lists as written.

```json
"Steps": [
  {
    "Id": "intune.devices-compliant", "Title": "Devices that sign in are compliant", "Summary": "...", "Product": "intune",
    "Goals": ["compliant-devices"], "Status": "NotDone", "Reason": null, "Readiness": "Blocked",
    "BlockedBy": ["intune.compliance-policies"], "Unconfirmed": [], "Unlocks": ["intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant"], "Rank": 4,
    "Tests": [],
    "Earlier": null,
    "Measure": { "Key": "devices-compliant", "Count": 412, "Total": 580, "Share": 71, "MinimumShare": 95, "Met": false,
                 "ReadAt": "2026-11-06T08:00:00Z", "Caveat": "...", "ObjectCount": 168,
                 "Objects": [{ "Type": "Device", "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }], "ReasonCode": null },
    "Requires": ["intune.compliance-policies"], "RequiresOneOf": [], "RecommendedFirst": ["intune.automatic-enrollment"],
    "Conflicts": [], "OnlyWhen": [], "Rollout": [], "Sources": [{ "Url": "...", "Mirror": "...", "Maintainer": null, "Note": "...", "Reviewed": "2026-11-05" }]
  }
],
"Goals": [
  { "Id": "compliant-devices", "Title": "Require compliant devices", "Summary": "...", "Step": "entra.ca-require-compliant-device",
    "Steps": ["entra.emergency-access-accounts", "..."], "Done": 3, "Applicable": 7, "Unknown": 1, "NotChecked": 2, "Status": "InProgress" }
]
```

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `Status` | `Done`, `NotDone`, `Unknown`, `NotChecked` or `NotApplicable`. `NotApplicable` when an `OnlyWhen` condition is false or every test that ran was skipped as `NotApplicable`; `NotDone` when a test failed or the measure is below its threshold; `Unknown` when nothing failed but a test ended as Investigate, Error or Skipped, the measure could not be read, or a condition could not be read; `Done` when every test that ran passed and the measure met its threshold; `NotChecked` when no test ran and no measure was read. |
| `Reason` | Why a step is `NotApplicable` (`ConditionNotMet`, `TestsNotApplicable`), `Unknown` (`ConditionUnknown`, or the first reason code of the tests or the measure, or `Investigate`) or `NotChecked` (`NotSelected` when it has tests, `MeasureOff` when the run config turned its measure off, `NoCheck` when it has neither). `null` otherwise. |
| `Readiness` | For a step that is `NotDone`, `Unknown` or `NotChecked`: `Blocked` (a required step is `NotDone`, every step of a "one of" group is `NotDone`, or a conflicting step is `Done`), `Unconfirmed` (not blocked, but a prerequisite is `Unknown` or `NotChecked`) or `Ready`. `null` for the other steps. |
| `BlockedBy`, `Unconfirmed` | The steps that block it, and the prerequisites still to check. |
| `Unlocks` | The steps in scope that depend on it directly and are not yet done. |
| `Rank` | The order every output lists steps in: Ready, Unconfirmed, Blocked, then Done and Not applicable; within each, prerequisites first, then by the urgency of the failed tests it holds up, then by ID. |
| `Tests` | Every test Maester knows that names the step, `{ Id, Result, ReasonCode }`. A test with no row in this result has `Result` `NotRun` and `ReasonCode` `NotInRun`. |
| `Earlier` | For a `NotChecked` step that an earlier run checked: `{ Status, ExecutedAt, File }`, from `Previous.LastKnown`. Never counted in this run's status. |
| `Measure` | For a step that is a state of the tenant: the figure read from Graph after the tests. `Share` is the whole percentage, rounded down; `Met` compares `Count` and `Total` with `MinimumShare` exactly. `Objects` holds up to 100 of the `ObjectCount` objects that fall short; they are also on the Affected objects page, with `Measure` among their sources. `ReasonCode` says why the figure could not be read: `ServiceNotConnected`, `LicenseNotFound`, `PermissionNotGranted` (the Graph connection lacks a permission it needs), `MeasureError` (the reader failed), or `MeasureOff` (the run config turned measures off). |
| Goal `Steps` | The goal's steps that are in scope, prerequisites first. `Done` and `Applicable` count them, leaving out those that are `NotApplicable`; `Unknown` and `NotChecked` count those. `Status` is `Done`, `NotStarted`, `InProgress`, or `NotApplicable` when no step applies. |

["""## 8. Selection
""", """### 7.4 Choices made in M3

Where the design was silent, M3 chose the simplest thing consistent with it. `website/docs/result-schema.md` documents
the result as built.

- **Reason codes.** `Reason` is also set for `NotApplicable` (`ConditionNotMet`, `TestsNotApplicable`) and `Unknown`
  (`ConditionUnknown`, else the first reason code of the tests or the measure, or `Investigate` for a test that ended
  as Investigate, which has no reason code). A measure that can't be read carries `ServiceNotConnected` or
  `LicenseNotFound` as a test would, and two codes tests don't have: `PermissionNotGranted` (the Graph connection lists
  its permissions and lacks every alternative of one; a 403 from the reader gives it too) and `MeasureError` (the
  reader threw). `MeasureOff` is the `ReasonCode` of a measure the run config turned off.
- **Mixed verifiers.** A test skipped as `NotApplicable` next to tests that gave a result is left out, not counted as
  Unknown. An `OnlyWhen` condition that can't be read makes the step Unknown before any test is looked at.
- **Readiness and Conflicts.** `BlockedBy` and `Unconfirmed` are both filled whatever the readiness, so a Blocked step
  still lists what is left to check. A conflicting step that is Unknown or Not checked is Unconfirmed. Conflicting
  steps are in scope (without their own prerequisites), so their status is known.
- **Rank.** Done steps follow the Blocked group, then Not applicable steps. Within a group, the order is topological
  over the edges between members of the group; among the steps that can come next, the highest value (own value
  plus unlock value) wins, then the ID.
- **Unlocks** lists the steps in scope that depend on the step directly and are not Done or Not applicable, in rank
  order.
- **Tests** always carry `ReasonCode` (`null` when none) and are sorted by ID with the numbers compared as numbers.
  A family test is left out when its instances have rows.
- **Measures.** `Share` is the whole percentage rounded down, so a step never shows 95% while it misses 95%; `Met`
  compares `Count` and `Total` exactly. With no object to count (`Total` 0), `Share` is `null` and `Met` is false:
  a compliant-device policy with no compliant device blocks everyone. Measures are read in `Invoke-Maester` right
  after the tests, while affected objects are still collected, and the readers write facts for the objects they
  list (source `Maester measures`): `device.managed`, `device.compliant`, `device.os`, `device.joinType`, and
  `user.mfaCapable` and `user.mfaRegistered` under the object ID and the UPN. The Affected objects page lists the
  same objects as `Steps[].Measure.Objects` (up to 100 per measure), with the source `Measure` and no test.
- **Goals.** A goal's `Steps` are its steps in scope, in catalogue order (prerequisites first). It also has
  `Summary`, `Unknown` and `NotChecked`, and `Status` `NotApplicable` when none of its steps applies.
- **Earlier** comes from all the `LastKnown` entries of a step's tests, judged by the status rules without measures;
  `ExecutedAt` and `File` are the newest entry's.
- **Tenant context.** The tenant context did not read `onPremisesSyncEnabled`. It now records it as `HybridIdentity`
  from the organization it already reads, with no extra request.
- **Selection.** `-IncludePrerequisites` is a second pass of `Resolve-MtNativePlan` (`-PrerequisiteStep`): the include
  selectors (`-TestId`, the typed selectors, `-Tag`) are lifted for tests of the prerequisites, and the exclusions
  (`-ExcludeTestId`, `-ExcludeProduct`, `-ExcludeTag`, a disabled or unlisted test) still apply. A long-running family
  keeps its long-running exclusion, which is how the Zero Trust family stays out without `-Suite ZTA` or
  `-IncludeLongRunning`. `Selection.Step` and `Selection.IncludePrerequisites` get no default in the resolved config,
  so a resolved config without them is unchanged.
- **Priority parity.** `Get-MtTestPriority` is checked against numbers computed with the report's formula. A test on
  the report side that compares its `priority()` with the same rows is for M4.

"""],
])

input.message:
M3 is committed on `claude/defenders-path-m3`, based on 3c3489712. Final commit: 83246182e1f05eabde61420bab29ac1e46c5f849. No pushes, PRs or GitHub posts. **Nothing has been run.** The worktree guard refused every `pwsh` command, so the code, the tests and the build are unverified. I checked the logic by reading it.

**Please run:**
1. `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Include 'DefendersPath*','MeasureReaders*','StepCatalog*','ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult*','Invoke-Maester.Selection*','ArgumentCompletion*','TestAttributes*','Convert-MtResultsToFlatObject*','ConsoleOutput*','Merge-MtMaesterResult*','Resolve-MtRunConfig*','Get-MtPesterSelectionPlan*','Help*','PSScriptAnalyzer*','RepositoryLayout*'`
2. `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1 -Exclude 'ZeroTrustAssessmentPack*' -ThrottleLimit 3`
3. `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`

**Shape of `Steps[]`:**
`{ Id, Title, Summary, Product, Goals[], Status (Done|NotDone|Unknown|NotChecked|NotApplicable), Reason, Readiness (Ready|Unconfirmed|Blocked|null), BlockedBy[], Unconfirmed[], Unlocks[], Rank, Tests:[{Id, Result, ReasonCode}], Earlier:{Status, ExecutedAt, File}|null, Measure, Requires, RequiresOneOf, RecommendedFirst, Conflicts, OnlyWhen, Rollout, Sources }`

`Measure` is exactly the fields in section 7.2: `{ Key, Count, Total, Share, MinimumShare, Met, ReadAt, Caveat, ObjectCount, Objects (up to 100 of {Type, Id, DisplayName}), ReasonCode }`.

**Shape of `Goals[]`:** `{ Id, Title, Summary, Step, Steps (the goal's steps in scope, prerequisites first), Done, Applicable, Unknown, NotChecked, Status (Done|NotStarted|InProgress|NotApplicable) }`

`Previous.LastKnown` is `{ <testId>: { Result, ReasonCode, ExecutedAt, File } }`.

**Deviations from section 7 (all recorded in the new design-doc section 7.4):**
- **Extra fields:** goals carry `Summary`, `Unknown` and `NotChecked`. Every `Tests` entry carries `ReasonCode`, `null` when there is none.
- **Reason codes:** `Reason` is also set for NotApplicable (`ConditionNotMet`, `TestsNotApplicable`) and for Unknown (`ConditionUnknown`, otherwise the first reason code, or `Investigate`).
- **New measure codes:** `PermissionNotGranted`, `MeasureError` and `MeasureOff`. The design said measures use the codes a skipped test uses, but tests have no permission gate.
- **Share and Met:** `Share` is rounded down. When `Total` is 0, `Share` is `null` and `Met` is false.
- **Goal scope:** a goal lists only its steps that are in scope, so its progress counts only those.
- **Conflicts:** conflicting steps are pulled into scope so their status is known.
- **Tenant context:** it did not actually read `onPremisesSyncEnabled`. It now records it as `HybridIdentity`, taken from the organization request it already makes.

**Public API changes:**
- `Invoke-Maester` gains `-Step` and `-IncludePrerequisites`.
- `Get-MtTest` gains `-Step`.
- Tab completion covers `-Step` on both commands.
- No new exported commands.
- Run config gains `Selection.Step`, `Selection.IncludePrerequisites`, `Measures.Enabled` and `Measures.MinimumShare.<key>`. `Resolve-MtRunConfig` rejects a threshold outside 1–100.
- The CSV gains `Step`, `Readiness` and `BlockedBy` columns.
- `SchemaVersion` is now `'2.2'`. There is no JSON schema file for results, so the bump is in the code, `result-schema.md` and `upgrading-from-2x.md`.

**Where things are:**
- **New internal functions:** `Get-MtStepPrerequisite`, `Get-MtStepScope`, `Invoke-MtStepMeasure` and `Get-MtMeasureSetting` in `powershell/internal/engine/`. `Get-MtResultStep` and `Get-MtTestPriority` in `powershell/internal/report/`.
- **Measures and facts:** measures are read in `Invoke-Maester` right after the tests, while affected objects are still collected. The two readers now write the device facts and `user.mfaCapable`/`user.mfaRegistered` (users under ID and UPN). `Measure` is exactly the fields in section 7.2: `{ Key, Count, Total, Share, MinimumShare, Met, ReadAt, Caveat, ObjectCount, Objects (up to 100 of {Type, Id, DisplayName}), ReasonCode }`.

**Deviations from section 7 (all recorded in the new design-doc section 7.4):**
- **Extra fields:** goals carry `Summary`, `Unknown` and `NotChecked`. Every `Tests` entry carries `ReasonCode`, `null` when there is none.
- **Reason codes:** `Reason` is also set for NotApplicable (`ConditionNotMet`, `TestsNotApplicable`) and for Unknown (`ConditionUnknown`, otherwise the first reason code, or `Investigate`).
- **New measure codes:** `PermissionNotGranted`, `MeasureError` and `MeasureOff`. The design said measures use the codes a skipped test uses, but tests have no permission gate.
- **Share and Met:** `Share` is rounded down. When `Total` is 0, `Share` is `null` and `Met` is false.
- **Goal scope:** a goal lists only its steps that are in scope, so its progress counts only those.
- **Conflicts:** conflicting steps are pulled into scope so their status is known.
